BiblicalUsage: Deker is named only once, as the father of Ben-deker, one of the twelve officers who supplied King Solomon's household from the hill country. His name survives inside his son's title, since the Hebrew text joins the two words as Ben-deker, and the token for Deker itself is listed under the word for son.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a name that appears once matters, because it belongs to a real man who served a real king. God keeps the record of faithful people the world forgets, and Deker's single verse is proof of it.
